item.title: Patrolling Pratas: From Peripheral Concern to a New Normal
item.description: CCG patrols around Pratas are steadily increasing.

item.title: USMCA Review 2026: Six Scenarios for North America’s Future
item.description: CSIS Americas Program Fellow Diego Marroquín Bitar and Senior Adviser and Scholl Chair Emeritus William Alan Reinsch explore and update a set of six potential scenarios for the future of the USMCA free trade agreement.

item.title: Europe Needs Bold Economic Action in the Face of the Iran Shock
item.description: As the war in Iran disrupts global energy markets, Europe cannot afford to wait. The European Union must launch a bold, collectively financed response—accelerating electrification, supporting Ukraine, and finally building a true European energy union.

item.title: Visualizing Iran’s Escalation Strategy
item.description: Iran is abandoning calibrated retaliation for rapid escalation—expanding the war across the region and raising stakes globally. The Middle East Program breaks down Tehran’s strategy with two new charts mapping horizontal and vertical escalation.

item.title: What the TotalEnergies Deal Means for Energy Investment, Political Risk, and Affordability
item.description: The Trump Administration’s $1 billion TotalEnergies deal does more than stop an offshore wind project—it establishes an executive precedent that bypasses Congress and courts, with far-reaching consequences for infrastructure investment across every sector.

item.title: Trendlines March 2026 Newsletter
item.description: This edition of Trendlines covers March 2026.

item.title: AI and Global Food Security: A Focus on Crop Breeding
item.description: AI promises to transform modern crop breeding, helping develop more resilient, nutritious, and higher-yielding crops with unprecedented pace—though barriers remain. CSIS experts unpack the benefits and risks of AI-enabled innovations for crop breeding around the world.

item.title: Clayton Seigle in NYT: Blockade Iran’s Oil
item.description: The best approach to curbing Iran’s oil exports is to impose a naval blockade of tankers carrying Iranian oil, writes CSIS’s Clay Seigle in The New York Times.
